runtime: Ubuntu (Linux 5.15), PowerShell 7.6.5, Microsoft.Graph 2.4.0 meta-module with Microsoft.Graph.Authentication 2.34.0 resolved on import, ExchangeOnlineManagement 3.10.0, ImportExcel not installed (CSV fallback path). Target: a small real tenant with no Microsoft 365 licences (11 members, 7 guests, 6 groups, no Teams, no mailboxes).
procedure: 1. Copy the script unchanged to a scratch directory so output stays out of the repository. 2. In one pwsh process, Import-Module Microsoft.Graph (unpinned), Connect-MgGraph -AccessToken with a delegated Graph token from an existing Azure CLI sign-in, and Connect-ExchangeOnline -AccessToken -Organization with a delegated Exchange token from the same sign-in. 3. Invoke the script with no parameters; it detects both existing sessions and skips device-code sign-in. 4. Cross-check each CSV row count against Graph $count queries (members, guests, all groups, Team-provisioned groups, mail-enabled groups) and against Get-EXOMailbox (all and SharedMailbox) in a separate session.
expected: The script reuses the existing Graph and EXO sessions, makes only Get-* calls, exits 0, and the CSV row counts equal the directly queried counts, including zero for object types the tenant does not have.
observed: Exit code 0 after about 5 seconds. Users 11 / Guests 7 / Groups 6 matched the Graph $count results exactly. Teams, TeamMembers, TeamOwners, SharedMailboxes, SharedMailboxPermissions, DistributionGroups and DLMembers were empty, which matched Graph (0 Team groups, 0 mail-enabled groups) and EXO (0 mailboxes, 0 shared mailboxes). With a token-based Graph session the log line 'Connected to Graph as' prints an empty account, and Disconnect-MgGraph writes the context object to the console. An earlier attempt failed at the script's own Import-Module Microsoft.Graph because the wrapper had pinned Microsoft.Graph 2.4.0 first, which loaded a conflicting Authentication assembly version; that failure came from the wrapper and not from the script.
limitations: The script's own device-code sign-in path was not exercised; sessions were pre-established with Azure CLI tokens.
The tenant has no Teams, mailboxes or distribution groups, so the per-Team member/owner loops, shared mailbox permission collection and DL member expansion ran over empty input and are not validated.
The ImportExcel workbook path was not exercised; only the CSV fallback ran.
Empty categories produce 0-byte CSV files without a header row, so 'none found' and 'not collected' look alike on disk; confirm with the run log.
Mixed Microsoft.Graph module versions installed side by side can break the script's unpinned Import-Module if another version is loaded earlier in the same session.
Performance and paging on a large tenant are not assessed. No tenant identifiers or exported rows are recorded here.
